text: just seen a guy at the library revising with his phone face down on a shelf behind him. no timer. no blockers. no forest. no screen time limits. just him and four hours of notes and a phone buzzing somewhere over his shoulder every few minutes. he flinched at every one. Absolute gladiator stuff.

text: i deleted instagram for the fourth time this year. no forest. no timer. no record of the eleven days i actually stayed off it. just me reinstalling at midnight like none of it ever counted. eleven days of effort and nothing left to show it happened. Brutal accounting honestly.
base_video: Creator in a dim bedroom, close-up, sat against the headboard holding a phone loosely, looking off to one side then slowly back to camera. Quiet, contemplative, no smile.
audio: slow ambient trending sound, low volume
caption: how many times have you deleted it
why_this_brand: The idea of a visible record of the sessions that did work is Forest's grown trees, not a generic willpower app.

text: my brother put his entire phone on greyscale to stop scrolling. no app blocking. no forest. no screen time limit. just a grey tiktok he watched for fifty minutes anyway. he said it felt less fun. he still finished the fifty minutes. Colour was never the problem.
base_video: Creator on a sofa, head tilted, eyebrows slightly raised, holding their own phone screen-down on their knee. One serious look at camera, one small tilt the other way.
caption: greyscale people, explain yourselves
why_this_brand: Free app blocking that protects the whole session, rather than dulling one feed, is Forest's Deep Focus.

text: watched a woman at the shared desk next to mine open instagram mid sentence. document still open. cursor still blinking. no blocker. no forest. no idea what she was writing. she sat there for nine minutes trying to remember the word she was going to type. then opened reddit to think about it. She's doing her best. it's not going great.
base_video: Creator at a kitchen table or co-working desk with a laptop open, looking slowly left, then right, then back to camera like they are searching the room for an explanation. No speaking.
caption: nine minutes for one word
why_this_brand: Slack in one tab and Instagram mid-task is the remote-worker app switching loop Forest's session timer sits on top of.

text: just seen a girl at the next table start a 25 minute pomodoro timer on youtube. on the same phone she is trying to stay off. no forest. no blockers. nothing between her and the sidebar. she is now fourteen minutes into a video about a man renovating a van. the timer is still running somewhere. Rest in peace to that study session.
base_video: Creator in a cafe or study space, coffee in frame, giving a slow questioning sideways glance off camera then blinking twice at the lens. Deliberately unimpressed.
caption: the sidebar gets everyone eventually
why_this_brand: A pomodoro timer running on the phone you are trying to ignore is the specific problem Forest's on-device timer and blocking solve.

text: sat through an entire family dinner last night with four phones face up on the table. no phone basket. no forest. no rule about it. no one even scrolling properly. just the odd flip of a screen and a nod at whoever was talking. we were all there. Nobody can confirm what anyone said.
base_video: Creator sat at a dinner table with plates and a couple of phones face up beside them, chewing slowly, looking straight at the camera with no expression, one small raise of the eyebrows.
audio: original audio, room tone (cutlery, muffled TV)
caption: phones face up at dinner, yes or no
why_this_brand: Forest's Plant Together shared session is built for exactly this table, where everyone is present and nobody is there.
